summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later lookup)

## BOOK 1: "In Sargasso." Missing, a romance (Julius Chambers, 1896, Transatlantic Publishing Co.)
Narrator/captain: **Capt. Austin Clark**, American from Brooklyn, 27-28 yrs old, commander of tramp steamer **Caribas** (owners Triplett & Jones, Plymouth; Caribas named after Marquis of that name; crew of 40, 2 years "Missing" at Lloyds).

**Preface**: Sargasso Sea = floating debris/seaweed, harbor of missing ships, "wonder-shop."

**Ch I-II**: Clark accepts passenger **Arthur Gray** (claims artist; has Secor launch, explosion-propelled). Sailed Harbeck's Stores, NY, June, bound Azores (Horta, Ponte Delgada, Lisbon). Gray urged course change at longitude 40. Sargasso bounds: lat 22-28N, long 25-60W. Clark's bosun/2nd mate; first mate left in charge. Clark sees mirage of derelicts in sky; lookout reports moving objects. Clark enters launch; Gray runs engine.

**Ch III**: Gray gets rifle (Winchester) under pretext of shooting fowl. Engine quits (false adjustment); oars dropped overboard. Gray lures Clark to derelicts. Clark's revolver empty; Clark drops cartridge belt in sea. Landing on ship's side hulk; Clark meets **the Kantoon** (60 yrs, grizzly gray beard trimmed 3 in., porpoise-skin dress, stands in barrel of water). Gray: "She is a fine boat... desirable accession."

**Ch IV**: Gray (wearing shark-skin clothes) reveals betrayal; had smallpox, adrift, rescued by Sargassons 5 yrs before. Sargasson rule: nobody escapes; "mercy of extinction." Gray claims oath, forsworn country. Clark locked in cell.

**Ch V**: Kantoon speaks polyglot ("Senor Captaine... Sitzen sie down"; "Io sono the Kantoon de cette ship"). Sargasson history: from Spanish Armada galleons; African slave ship mutineers early 1800s; Sacred Light; life of ship ~50 yrs; drowning when ship sinks; children tossed; death chant. Clark overhears plan to take Caribas that night.

**Ch VI**: Red blood-colored "Sacred Fire" light (locomotive headlight on iron hulk, Priest of Sacred Fire). Clark fed by unknown woman (wicker dish of boiled seaweed). Boats: grass-matting canoes, paddles like tennis bats. Attack plan: Tabasco-like red pepper dust + opium-like fungus drug in fish bladders; Winchester held by Gray's boat; 200 attackers; Gray guides; 50 miles in ~8 hrs. Attack on Caribas mooring at hulk; boatswain (superstitious, sounded no eight bells, woke crew, whistle) defended; ~dozen killed; cabin boy dropped feet first tied with weight; boatswain drowned in water butt by Kantoon's order (he chose drowning). Caribas steam banked; Kantoon gives Clark binoculars.

**Ch VII**: Kantoon narrates; cabin boy and 2nd mate killed; crew knocked and tossed. Clark's sorrow.

**Ch VIII**: **Fidette** (Kantoon's daughter; hazel-brown eyes, reddish-brown hair; Creole French; sprig of rhododendron/bay; wicker tray of berries). Mother from New Orleans (daughter of a placée; eloped with gambler son of sugar planter; Summer 1872 steamer "George Cornwall", Capt. Timothy Rogers, lost; mother alone on derelict 5 months; captured; Kantoon chose her as his prize; married by Deputy Chief Kantoon). Clark kisses Fidette.

**Ch IX**: Kantoon angry; threatens separation; Kantoon's wife dead 6 months (fever). Social structure: Kantoon only man allowed wife; dry-rot fear; barnacle-sinking bark; "Repose is the conception of Sargasson excitement." Food: seaweed pudding, fish; seaweed cigarettes; wife-abuse punishment; death by D-shaped bending & sea.

**Ch X**: Clark guards Fidette's swim (spear on board, sharks). Visit to cook ship (fires only there). Barnacle soup. Caribas seen moored in new slip.

**Ch XI**: Fidette's first love: **Don Fernandez Otranto**, son of exiled Portuguese marshal, trombone player, escaped from Royal George... Goo-ge-Goo / "Green Octopod" sunk by jealous hunchbacked Kantoon's daughter. Trombone music heard — Fernandez alive.

**Ch XII-XIII**: Jealousy; "Week of Silence" festival (sleep week; Sun Dance; Dance of the Derelicts). Fidette's Bantang.

**Ch XIV**: Fernandez visits; Fidette douses him; Kantoon has him drowned in sack. Fidette shows no remorse.

**Ch XV**: Women's visitation ("Month of the Visitation"); women weigh under 200 lbs rule; Chin-Goone revolt (1816, scuttled 100 ships; Napoleon rescue plot). Virginius/Wabash anecdote.

**Ch XVI**: Papier-mâché orange bombs (fireworks from Wilmington, Del.) in Kantoon's cabin; Clark's Brandywine explosion memory. Hansko Yap rebel (rejected height, 6ft rule), spar-battering-ram attack.

**Ch XVII**: Spar fight; Kantoon killed by Lascar (hobbled); Clark's rope fender.

**Ch XVIII**: Fidette climbs rigging, throws bombs; Hansko Yap's men killed. Fidette saves ship.

**Ch XIX**: Kantoon buried; Clark marries Fidette (civil ceremony around mainmast; baptism by rain water).

**Ch XX**: Clark makes new boats (root matting, fish-scale gum); root telegraph; Clark cooks barnacle chowder.

**Ch XXI**: Priest's barge Unk-ta-hee; High Priest's floating monastery; Chief Kantoon; oath with glowing marlinspike; Clark given Caribas.

**Ch XXII-XXIII**: Ceremony; Clark retakes Caribas from Gray's successor; Gray, now in captain's cabin tied in chair.

**Ch XXIV**: Gray drowned in his own kneeling chair ("Let him walk with God"). Gray says Clark can never escape. Gray scuttled Secor launch.

**Ch XXV-XXVI**: Donna Elenora (wife of Kantoon of Cormorant) and Fidette's "women's rights" propaganda; gig; Sacred Flint stolen (Elenora borrowed it via Chief Kantoon's daughter); Clark's ballast flint trick.

**Ch XXVII-XXVIII**: Sacred Fire flashed; Clark sends 20 boats of flint. Escape plan: porpoise oil, seaweed fuel, barnacle-smoke concealment, eight stokers padlocked, boatswain ally, provisions: 50 barrels salt pork, 100 barrels crackers. A crew member missing.

**Ch XXIX-XXX**: Knife-grinder song; crew knives collected. Engine starts after sulphuric acid in cylinder. Escape via Grand Canal; sank barge with 30 men. Sacred Fire: "The Caribas is gone! Her Kantoon shall die." Two days north; fuel out; German steamer **Nordland** (Gibraltar→NY) rescues; anchored NY Horseshoe. Telegram from Triplett & Jones: "Proceed Santos, then Buenos Ayres for orders." END.

---

## BOOK 2: Poppy Ott's Pedigreed Pickles (Leo Edwards, 1927, Grosset & Dunlap; illus. Bert Salg)
Narrator **Jerry Todd** (Tutter, La Salle County, Illinois); friend **Poppy Ott** (long-legged, schemer, earlier stilt factory, Seven-League Stilts). Poppy's father Mr. Ott (shiftless once; now runs stilt factory). Jerry's mother and father (Dad, Mother); Doc Leland (pill case, big nose glasses, Lizzie car). Marshal **Bill Hadley**.

**Ch I**: Poppy proposes Pickle Parlor; empty store rent $125/mo from Pennykorn; overheard Canners Exchange Bank talk: Mr. Foreman Pennykorn (president), son Norman Pennykorn (runs canning factory), grandson **Forrest Pennykorn** (snob, roadster). Ashton Canning Co. competitor. Dandy Dills pickles. Cashier Mr. Blynn.

**Ch II**: Poppy's pickles from Presbyterian missionary food sale at Drake's store; **Mrs. Clayton** (housekeeper of **Mr. Simon Weckler**, widower, stoop-shouldered, cane, cat **Peter**, yellow). Weckler's playhouse offered; rent $5/mo; Weckler is "silent partner," pay in pickles. Cat rescued from cistern by Poppy.

**Ch III**: Floor plan; $50 each; account at Mr. Thomas Lorring's bank (Commercial Bank). Sign: "Poppy's Pickle Parlor." Ad "WHOSE PICKLES" — diamond line mistake (seven diamonds worth $10,000).

**Ch IV**: 63 letters; Peoria police chief telegram (diamond robbery); Bill Hadley. Mrs. Morgan, Mrs. Hempline, Mrs. Cook, Mrs. Hiram Springer; broom-swatting woman.

**Ch V**: Butch McGinty (Zulutown, towing, mule Jerusalem; burns cookies); Poppy and Jerry hire him at $3.50/day. Pickle genius = Butch.

**Ch VI**: Aunt Jemima scheme; royalty refused; Butch's recipe secret.

**Ch VII**: Widow **Cora O'Mally** (old Weir house in river bottoms, two-foot walls, big chimney, cucumber patch; pirate **Peg-leg Weir**). Cellar sounds, O'Mally frightened.

**Ch VIII**: River swim; Jerry loses pants; canning truck driver **Pennykorn's employee** ("smarty" = Forrest) at O'Mally's; O'Mally sells 4 bushels to Poppy & Jerry at $2/bushel. Pickling at Poppy's house; Mr. Ott at wedding (nephew Henny). Samples: 300 bottles, "AUNT JEMIMA'S PICKLES" handbill.

**Ch IX**: Ptomaine poisoning from stuffed olives at church supper; Mrs. Brown; Mr. Weckler's store moved to lot across from cannery; Pennykorn claims lot.

**Ch X**: Jerry blames Butch but poisoning real cause was church olives (Miz Higgins). Expense book total $68. Mr. Weckler attacked (library, bloody head); one-armed burglar; gold cucumber (lead pocket piece) found.

**Ch XI**: Cat killer (strangled Peter). Mr. Hartenbower (centenarian) story of iron mold/gold cucumbers. Spider Whickleberry's mechanical cat-catcher (revealed later).

**Ch XII**: Poppy ordered 700 bushels from O'Mally at $2/bushel via Rockford cousin Henny & Wiggins & Wakefield. O'Mally cellar: 130 bushels.

**Ch XIII**: Pennykorn offers O'Mally 90¢; O'Mally says sold at $2. Threats. Jerry: "Monkey-face."

**Ch XIV**: Secret tunnel; Cap'n Tinkertop's boat; creek; cement tunnel; Mrs. O'Mally's Weir house.

**Ch XV**: Midnight: cat strangled in chimney base, tail cut; secret iron door; Poppy knocks out **Tommy Weir** (grandson of Weckler, son of Nathan Weir).

**Ch XVI**: Uncle Abner Weir (Rimtown, Ohio; one-armed? no—Nathan is one-armed). Cave; Tommy; Tommy's ill-fated cat-killing machine; uncle's Bible lessons; cave stove.

**Ch XVII**: Uncle Abner's story: Peg-leg Weir's treasure; gold cucumber key; Nathan Weir; Tommy's mother died; gold cucumber stolen by cat killer.

**Ch XVIII**: Pickles made by Mrs. O'Mally (her recipe, which Butch had); Ladies' Aid (Methodist; Presbyterian; Catholic); loan $500 from Lorring; "Poppy's Pedigreed Pickles."

**Ch XIX**: Kegs; Pennykorn letter to Wiggins & Wakefield (warning about ptomaine). Farmer's cucumbers ordered by Uncle Abner. Pennykorn offers $200 bonus + assume debts; Jerry refuses.

**Ch XX**: Poppy's telegram; Weckler reunion with Tommy (Clara = daughter, eloped). Bank confrontation; Bill Hadley at window; Poppy sold to railroad president Mr. **Lorrimer** and Chicago hotels (orders ~$6,000+).

**Ch XXI**: Treasure in chest by moon/chimney shadow (~2 AM). Tom's gold cucumber halves; drawings: sun/moon, clock at 12, chimney, coffin. Each partner $7,000; total $35,000. Newspaper photo.

**Ch XXII**: Lorring; Pennykorn stock deal; Chamber of Commerce banquet; Poppy's silent speech; Mrs. O'Mally and Uncle Abner married; Nathan Weir in penitentiary, Peoria jewel robbery; Spider Whickleberry; cat killer died in hospital. Next book: POPPY OTT AND THE FRECKLED GOLDFISH.
